intro: You're looking for a bookkeeper who works in Xero and is local to you, probably because you want someone who can handle the day-to-day bookkeeping in the software you already use. You might be setting up Xero for the first time, or you've fallen behind and want a nearby professional to take it on. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK bookkeeper who can quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a Xero bookkeeper near me usually need
need_lead: People want a local bookkeeper who knows Xero inside out and can take the stress out of keeping the books straight.
needs: You've just started using Xero and want a bookkeeper who can set up bank feeds and rules properly from the beginning.
Your bookkeeping has slipped and you need someone nearby to catch up on reconciliation and invoicing in Xero.
You run a small business and want a local bookkeeper to manage Xero day to day so you can get on with the work.
You're moving from another system to Xero and need a bookkeeper who can transfer your records and keep everything tidy.
You want someone you can meet or speak to locally who understands Xero's reporting and can help you make sense of your figures.
context_heading: What to understand about Xero bookkeepers near you
context: Bookkeeping isn't a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct. You can ask any bookkeeper you speak to which body supervises them.

Xero bookkeepers are trained in Xero's bank feeds, rules, invoicing and reporting, and many are Xero certified advisors. That certification is worth asking about because it shows a bookkeeper has demonstrated their Xero knowledge. A good bookkeeper will also be clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice.

faqs.q: What does a Xero bookkeeper near me actually do?
faqs.a: A Xero bookkeeper handles the day-to-day recording of your income and expenses in Xero, including bank feeds, reconciliation, invoicing and reporting. They may also help you set up bank rules and add-on apps to speed things up. They don't usually prepare year-end accounts or give tax advice, which is an accountant's role.

faqs.q: Do I need a bookkeeper who is Xero certified?
faqs.a: It's not a legal requirement, but Xero certification shows a bookkeeper has demonstrated their knowledge of the software. Many bookkeepers are Xero certified advisors, and it's a reasonable question to ask. Certification doesn't replace proper supervision for anti-money-laundering purposes, so check that too.

faqs.q: How do I check a bookkeeper is properly supervised?
faqs.a: Anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. You can ask which body supervises them and confirm membership with that body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) also shows they've trained to a recognised standard.

faqs.q: Can a Xero bookkeeper help if I'm behind on my bookkeeping?
faqs.a: Yes, many bookkeepers can catch up on overdue work, often called a clean-up, and get your Xero records up to date. It's worth telling them how far back the work goes when you enquire. They can then quote you for the catch-up and ongoing support.
